kjv: For now I will stretch out my hand, that I may smite thee
mine: For by now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you
note: shalahti is perfect with 'attah ("by now"), used counterfactually: God could already have wiped Pharaoh out (and v.16 explains why he has not). The KJV turns it into a future threat that is never carried out.

kjv: for this [cause] have I raised thee up
mine: for this reason I have let you remain
note: he'emadtika (hiphil of 'amad) means "I have caused you to stand / kept you standing", i.e. let you survive; "raised thee up" (cf. Rom 9:17, exegeira) can suggest bringing Pharaoh to power.
qolot 'elohim is literally "voices/thunders of God"; the KJV takes 'elohim as a superlative ("mighty"), a possible idiom, but the plain sense ties the thunder to God.
kussemet is spelt or emmer wheat, a grain grown in Egypt; rye was not cultivated there.
